title: How to Get an OFW Medical Exam (PEME)
description: Complete the mandatory Pre-Employment Medical Examination (PEME) at DOH-accredited clinics for your overseas deployment.

content.title: What is the OFW Medical Exam (PEME)?

blocks.content: The **Pre-Employment Medical Examination (PEME)** is a mandatory health screening for all Filipinos planning to work abroad. It ensures that the worker is physically and mentally fit to perform their duties in the host country and meets the health standards set by the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) and the Department of Health (DOH).

The Medical Exam is commonly used for:
*   Requirement for OEC/OFW Pass issuance
*   Visa application for certain countries (e.g., South Korea, Taiwan, Gulf countries)
*   Company compliance for the foreign employer

You may need an OFW Medical Exam if you are:
- A first-time OFW (Land-based or Sea-based)
- A returning OFW with a new contract or employer
- A seafarer renewing their medical certificate

content.title: Benefits of Having a PEME Certificate

blocks.content: Completing your medical exam at an accredited clinic ensures your deployment is legal and your health is protected.

blocks.title: Legal Compliance
blocks.content: The DMW will not issue your exit clearance without a "Fit to Work" status uploaded by an accredited clinic.

blocks.title: Health Awareness
blocks.content: The comprehensive exam can detect underlying conditions (like high blood sugar or hypertension) before you leave, allowing you to seek treatment in the Philippines.

blocks.title: Agency Referral
blocks.content: If you have a recruitment agency, they will usually direct you to a specific accredited clinic.

blocks.title: Wafid System (For GCC Countries)
blocks.content: For those bound for the Middle East, you must register at [Wafid.com](https://wafid.com) to be assigned to a clinic.
**Pro Tip:** The **DMW Mobile App** is now the primary portal for OEC and e-Registration. Ensure your profile is 100% complete before booking appointments.

blocks.title: Find an Accredited Clinic
blocks.content: Check the list of DOH-accredited OFW clinics. If bound for the GCC, follow the Wafid assignment.

blocks.title: Prepare for the Exam
blocks.content: Fast for 8–10 hours. Get enough sleep and avoid drinking alcohol or taking unnecessary medication 24–48 hours before the test.

blocks.title: Registration at the Clinic
blocks.content: Arrive early (usually 7:00 AM to 8:00 AM). Present your passport, photos, and referral slip. Pay the medical fee.

blocks.title: Undergo Medical Tests
blocks.content:
The exam typically includes:
*   **Laboratory:** Blood tests (HIV, Hep B/C, Syphilis), Urinalysis, and Stool exam.
*   **Imaging:** Chest X-ray.
*   **Physical:** Vision (Ishihara), Hearing, BP, and General Physical Exam.
*   **Psychological:** A mandatory personality and psychological evaluation.

blocks.title: Wait for Results
blocks.content: Results are usually ready within **24 to 72 hours**. If you are "Fit to Work," the clinic will upload your results directly to the DMW system.

Applicants may process their Medical Exam at:
- **DOH-Accredited OFW Clinics:** Mostly located in Manila (Ermita/Malate), Cebu, and Davao.
- [Wafid Portal](https://wafid.com) (For GCC registration).

Typical processing timelines include:
*   Examination: 4–6 Hours
*   Results Release: 1–3 Working Days
You can check your medical status on the **DMW Online Services Portal** or by contacting the clinic directly.

Applicants may experience:
- **Hazy X-ray:** Often caused by a recent cough or cold. You may be asked to undergo "Sputum Testing" which can take weeks.
- **High Blood Sugar/BP:** Can lead to a "Temporary Unfit" status until the condition is controlled.

items: **Using a non-accredited clinic:** Your results will not be recognized by the DMW.
**Lying about medical history:** If discovered during the exam or abroad, it can lead to deportation or being banned from working overseas.

blocks.content: Always ensure the name on your medical certificate exactly matches your passport.

items: Drink plenty of water in the days leading up to your exam.
If you have a pre-existing condition (like Diabetes), bring your latest doctor's clearance and maintenance meds.
Avoid salty and fatty foods 3 days before the exam.

blocks.title: How long is the medical certificate valid?
blocks.content: Most OFW medical certificates are valid for **three (3) months** from the date of issuance.

blocks.title: What if I get an "Unfit to Work" result?
blocks.content: You will be given a chance to undergo treatment or "re-evaluation" depending on the condition. Some conditions (like HIV or Hepatitis B for certain countries) are permanent disqualifications.
